ORAL COMMUNICATION
Members of the public may address the City Council at this time. No action will be taken on non-agenda
items at this meeting. Speakers should limit comments to two (2) minutes each.

CONSENT CALENDAR

1.  City Council Minutes
  Although the live recording is the official record of public meetings, minutes are prepared for the
  Council’s approval.
  Recommended Action
  Approve minutes from the February 18, 2025 regular City Council Meetings.

2.  Warrants
  Expenditures Submitted for Approval:
  • US Bank General Account Warrants totaling $496,918.33.
  • One payroll totaling $253,210.33.
  • One electronic fund transfer totaling $3,133.70.
  Recommended Action
  Approve total expenditures for February 10, 2025 through February 21, 2025 totaling
  $753,262.36.

3.  Adoption an Ordinance Repealing and Replacing Title 4, Public Safety, Chapter 4-1 Bicycles
  and Repealing Chapter 4-10 of the Avalon Municipal Code
  On February 4, 2025, City Council introduced and waived all readings of an ordinance to repeal
  and replace Title 4, Chapter 4-1 and repeal Chapter 4-10 of the Avalon Municipal Code. The
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
MARCH 4, 2025

  proposed ordinance covers requirements of licensing, operation, and enforcement provisions for
  bicycles and electric bicycles.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt an Ordinance of the City of Avalon Repealing and Replacing Title 4, Chapter 4-1 and
  Repealing Chapter 4-10 of the Avalon Municipal Code Regarding Bicycles, Electric Bicycles and
  Motorized Bicycles.

4.  Fire Surplus Equipment
  Historically, the City Council is presented with a list of items that are surplus, the Council declares
  it surplus, and then the declared items are either sold via Public Surplus, given to charity, or
  disposed of properly.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution declaring vehicles & equipment listed in resolution as surplus property and
  authorize the City Manager to dispose of it in accordance with City policy.

PUBLIC HEARING

5.  Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Miscellaneous Fee Schedule Revisions
  The City charges fees for miscellaneous public services, use of City facilities and equipment
  rental and other activities. Since the adoption of the fee schedule, City Staff would like to propose
  the following new fees to be added.
  Recommended Action
  1. Hear a presentation regarding the Miscellaneous Fee Schedule. 2. Open the Public Hearing
  to hear public comments. 3. Close the Public Hearing. 4. If consensus, adopt the fee schedule
  as proposed.

GENERAL BUSINESS

6.  Presentation and Discussion on Revisions to Avalon Municipal Code § 4-4 Vehicles
  City staff are presenting considerations for City Council that introduce modernized definitions,
  permit categories, and administrative procedures while preserving core public safety and
  operational standards.
  Recommended Action
  Receive a presentation to consider updates to Avalon Municipal Code § 4-4 Vehicles and provide
  direction on revisions.

ADJOURN

NOTICE OF POSTING

I, Devin Elise Hart, declare that the City Council Agenda for Tuesday, March 4, 2025 was posted on
Friday, February 28, 2025 on the City’s website, www.cityofavalon.com/aqendacenter, and at City Hall,
410 Avalon Canyon Road.

Devin Elise Hart, Senior Management Analyst

7.  Patrol Boat 4 Hull Repairs and Paint
  1. Made the affirmative finding that the City will not gain a competitive advantage
  by using the formal contract bid or other competitive procedure and dispense with
  formal bidding or other competitive procedures as outlined in Avalon Municipal
  Code Section 3-4.106.
  2. Authorized the City Manager to approve an expenditure not to exceed $30,000,
  from the Harbor Capital Improvement budget, account 10470-6781, for major
  repairs and refurbishment to be done to the hull of Patrol Boat 4.
  Motion to approve made by Lisa Lavelle, seconded by Michael Ponce. (All Ayes)

  agreement with MKS Specialty Finishes, Inc., and Geoff King Plumbing, to perform
  renovation work to the public restrooms located at the Green Pier at a cost not to
  exceed $100,000 from the Green Pier Restrooms CIP fund (10470-6547) Project

  Motion to approve made by Michael Ponce, seconded by Yesenia De La Rosa.
  (All Ayes)

  Investigation, Corrective Action Plan and Verification Monitoring for Underground
  Storage Tank Site at the Ava Ion Fuel Dock

  Agreement with Wayne Perry, Inc. for a not to exceed amount of $60,000 for Site
  Assessment, Soil and Water Investigation, Corrective Action Plan and Verification
  Monitoring for underground storage tank site at the Avalon Fuel Dock.
  Motion to approve made by Michael Ponce, seconded by Mary Schickling.
  (All Ayes)

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Adopt an Ordinance of the City of Avalon Repealing and
Replacing Title 4, Chapter 4-1 and Repealing Chapter 4-10 of the Avalon Municipal Code
Regarding Bicycles, Electric Bicycles and Motorized Bicycles.

REPORT SUMMARY: On February 4, 2025 City Council introduced and waived all
readings of an ordinance to repeal and replace Title 4, Chapter 4-1 and repeal Chapter
4-10 of the Avalon Municipal Code.

The proposed ordinance covers requirements of licensing, operation, and enforcement
provisions for bicycles and electric bicycles. Perhaps most notably in the ordinance is the
ability for local law enforcement to securely store bicycles, e-bicycles, and illegal off-
highway vehicles/motorcycles for violations of the proposed municipal code amendment.

At this meeting, the City Council is asked to adopt the ordinance.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Unknown.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Health and Safety

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City and
Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department will not have the support of the Avalon
Municipal Code to further regulate bicycles, electric bicycles, and motorized bicycles.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Publish ordinance and update the Avalon Municipal Code.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: The item was properly listed on the
posted agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

§ 4-1 -102. Definitions.
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall have the
meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a
different meaning:
  (a) Bicycle: Any device upon which a person may ride which is propelled by human

  (b) Bicycle Plate: The license tag or decal designated by the State in accordance
  with California Vehicle Code § 39001 to be permanently affixed to the bicycle and

  (c) Electric Bicycle: An electric bicycle is a bicycle equipped with fully operable
  pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, and is categorized by the
  following:
  (1) Class 1 electric bicycle is equipped with a motor that provides
  assistance only when the rider is pedaling, and that ceases to provide
  assistance when the bicycle reaches a speed of 20 miles per hour.
  (2) Class 2 electric bicycle is equipped with a motor that may be used
  exclusively to propel the bicycle, and that is not capable of providing
  assistance when the bicycle reaches a speed of 20 miles per hour.
  (3) Class 3 electric bicycle is equipped with a motor that provides
  assistance only when the rider is pedaling, and that ceases to provide
  assistance when the bicycle reaches a speed of 28 miles per hour.
  This bicycle is equipped with a speedometer.
  (d) Motorized Bicycle: Any two-wheeled or three-wheeled device having fully
  operative pedals for propulsion by human power, or having no pedals if powered
  solely by electrical energy, and an automatic transmission and a motor which
  produces less than four gross brake horsepower and is capable of propelling the
  device at a maximum speed of not more than 30 miles per hour on level ground.
  (e) Off-Highway Vehicle: Any two, three, or four wheeled device with no pedals that
  attains speeds of greater than 20 miles per hour or 750 watts of power that is
  illegal to operate on a public roadway. This include vehicles commonly referred
  to as electric motorcycles, all-terrain vehicles, or dirt bikes.

All bicycles, electric bicycles, and motorized bicycles must be registered by the owner

condition.

information to the Vehicle Clerk.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City charges fees for miscellaneous public services, use of City
facilities and equipment rental and other activities. User fees are assessed and collected for City
services and programs provided by various departments. These are services that convey a
benefit, grant a privilege, provide for review and enforcement of regulatory activities, enforce
laws, or are a condition of development. Under State law, cities may charge fees to recoup the
direct and indirect costs related to the provision of user services.

Each year, the City reviews its fees to establish new fees, modify existing fees, and eliminate
fees that are no longer required to ensure that City fees are in-line with the costs incurred to
provide them.

On June 4, 2024, City Council approved a 3.90% increase for the majority of fees effective July
1, 2024, with the exception of transit and certain recreation fees. The percentage increase was
based on the consumer price index (CPI) information provided by the Bureau of Labor Statistics
for Los Angeles County based on the latest available fiscal year information. Using the CPI as
an average cost increase annually ensures the city does not unnecessarily burden the citizens
with unusually large spikes in fees while also ensuring that the City continues to recoup costs
associated with the increased costs to provide these services.

Since the adoption of the fee schedule, City Staff would like to propose the following new fees
to be added:

 City Staff would like to also propose the removal of the combined scheduled annual service fee
as the personnel and equipment may vary depending on the location and nature of required

SUBJECT:  Presentation and Discussion on Revisions to Avalon
  Municipal Code § 4-4 Vehicles

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Receive a presentation to consider updates to Avalon
Municipal Code § 4-4 Vehicles and provide direction on revisions.

REPORT SUMMARY: Per California Vehicle Code 21100.5, the City of Avalon is uniquely
bestowed the authority to manage and regulate vehicles including the size, number,
vehicle class, noise limits, and maximum speed limits.

The City’s vehicle regulations have been in place for several decades with revisions every
few years, addressing vehicle classifications, permits, and enforcement. Recent changes
in vehicle technology, increased transportation demands, and evolving community
expectations necessitate a comprehensive review. City staff are presenting
considerations for City Council that introduce modernized definitions, permit categories,
and administrative procedures while preserving core public safety and operational
standards. Below are items staff is seeking discussion and direction on before returning
to City Council with a draft ordinance.

  1. Definitions and Classifications:
  • More detailed definitions in a centralized location at the beginning of the code
  to clearly distinguish between vehicle types and terminology. Enhance clarity
  for both enforcement and public understanding.
  • Consider changing Microcar Length from 120.1” to 135” to accommodate “Kei”
  trucks without modification and Oversize from 200” to 215” to acknowledge
  larger full size vehicle standards (currently 71 residential vehicles oversize).
  • Aflow residents in ADUs and JADU5 to qualify for Residential Autoette.
  • Allow Vehicle Hearing Officer to approve requests for more than 1 Residential
  Autoette for Senior and/or Disabled Roommate Living accommodations.

  2. Permit Structure and Limitations:
  • Add a Residential Motorcycle Permit definition (to include motorized scooters)
  and limit 1 per dwelling unit.
  • Consider explicit limits (for example, no more than ## residential vehicle
  permits or ## commercial vehicle permits).
   o  Or, continue issuing 2 for 1 residential vehicle permits (blue sticker) and
  1 for 1 commercial vehicle permits.
  o And/or, set caps at today’s current issuance (including autoettes) with a
  1 for 1 replacement for all vehicle types.
  •  More clearly outline a waitlist mechanism to manage demand more equitably
  and determine feasibility of “banking” stickers.
  o Consider Annual Waitlist Renewal
  o Currently 41 autoette vehicles with Residential Blue Sticker and 34
  permits renewed annually with no associated vehicle.
  •  Align overnight parking regulation hours (non-residential midnight to 6:00 am
  and commercial 7:00 pm to 6:00 am).
  o Current Code requires Oversized Vehicles Park Off-Street (although not
  readily known or enforced).
  •  Address the Use of “Floaters” not currently in Code.

  3. Replacement and Transfer Provisions:
  • Allow Legacy permits to continue as long as renewed annually and on-time
  (currently totals roughly 128 residential vehicle permits).
  • Clearly delineate replacement conditions, including restrictions for oversized
  vehicles and mandates that commercial autoettes or rental autoettes be
  replaced with certified electric vehicles.
  • Refine Transfer provisions, particularly for residential vehicle permits, to
  address situations such as death, dissolution of marriage, or intergenerational
  transfers regardless of when a permit was originally secured.
  • Consider transfers to full-time Residents or Real Property Owners.

  4. Administrative and Enforcement Enhancements:
  • Assign clear responsibilities to the Vehicle Clerk and Vehicle Hearing Officer,
  ensuring a more consistent application of the regulations.
  • Outline enhanced enforcement measures (e.g., detailed procedures for
  citations and fines for non-compliance), which are designed to better address
  repeat violations and unauthorized vehicles.

  5. Additional Considerations:
  • Create Residential Parking Program (by neighborhood application) ordinance.
  • Clarify Electrification Requirement for Commercial Autoette and Commercial
  Rental Autoette.
  • Modify AMC 9-7-606 (a) Parking Space Dimensions (current autoette parking
  space is outdated at: 6’ in width x 10’ in length).

After input and public comment, staff expect to return to City Council at a later date with
a draft ordinance for further discussion and review. Any requested changes would be
reviewed by the City Attorney to make sure they are compliant with the Vehicle Code and
any due process or property rights.

additional modifications or clarifications. Upon Council direction, staff will prepare a first
reading ordinance amendment package at a future Council meeting and/or Town Hall.
